23 Which wave is a longitudinal wave?
A
a light wave travelling through air
B
a radio wave from a broadcasting station
C
a ripple on the surface of water
D
a sound wave travelling through air

hints: Recall the test for this question: in a longitudinal wave the particles oscillate parallel to energy travel, in a transverse wave they oscillate perpendicular to travel.
Group the four examples: light travelling through air and radio from a broadcasting station are both electromagnetic waves, which are always transverse.
Compare the remaining two: a water surface ripple moves particles up-down for horizontal travel, while sound in air moves air molecules back-and-forth along the travel direction as pressure changes.
walkthrough: Identify the definition needed: a longitudinal wave has displacement of the medium parallel to the direction of propagation, forming compressions and rarefactions.
Check the light wave travelling through air and the radio wave from a broadcasting station: both are part of the electromagnetic spectrum.
Electromagnetic waves are transverse because the oscillating electric and magnetic fields are perpendicular to the direction of energy transfer, so neither can be longitudinal.
Check the ripple on the surface of water: the water surface moves vertically up and down while the ripple energy spreads horizontally, which is perpendicular motion and therefore transverse.
Check the sound wave travelling through air: vibrating air molecules oscillate back and forth along the same line as the wave travels, producing pressure compressions and rarefactions.
That parallel oscillation matches the definition of a longitudinal wave, so the sound wave is the only longitudinal example. This is option D

A.explanation: A light wave is an electromagnetic wave with oscillations perpendicular to travel, so it is transverse not longitudinal.

B.explanation: A radio wave is an electromagnetic wave, so its electric and magnetic oscillations are transverse to the direction of travel.

C.explanation: A ripple on water has surface particles moving up and down while the wave travels horizontally, so it is transverse.

D.explanation: A sound wave in air is a series of compressions and rarefactions with air particles oscillating parallel to travel, so it is longitudinal.
